title: Cocktail 2 Just Crossed ₹128 Crore Worldwide — and Shahid Kapoor Finally Has His Comeback
excerpt: Nine days, ₹75 crore in India, a chemistry experiment between Shahid, Kriti Sanon, and Rashmika Mandanna that actually worked — and now the only question is whether the ₹100-crore club will open its doors before Welcome to the Jungle steals the screens.
body:
Here's the thing about **Cocktail 2**: nobody was supposed to care this much.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=XXxUqLHq1xg</youtube>

A sequel to a fourteen-year-old romantic comedy, arriving in the most brutally competitive month Bollywood has seen in years, fronted by a lead actor whose last theatrical outing (*O Romeo*, February 2026) netted a painful ₹8.50 crore on opening day before vanishing from multiplexes. On paper, **Shahid Kapoor** was walking into a fight he wasn't favoured to win.

Nine days later, the film has crossed **₹128 crore worldwide** and is sitting at roughly **₹75 crore net in India**. The ₹100-crore domestic mark — once a fantasy for this project — is now a genuine conversation.

## The Numbers Tell a Story

The trajectory has been unusually healthy. A **₹13.5 crore** opening day signalled that audiences were genuinely curious, not just showing up out of obligation. The weekend pushed the domestic total past ₹50 crore, and — this is the part that matters — the weekday drops were controlled. Monday held at ₹6.75 crore. Tuesday matched it. By the time the first week closed at roughly **₹70.50 crore net**, the film had already crossed the original *Cocktail*'s lifetime collection of ₹74.50 crore (unadjusted).

The second Friday brought in another **₹3.50 crore**, a strong hold that suggests word-of-mouth is still doing its work. Trade estimates now peg the second weekend addition at ₹11-14 crore, which would push the India net past **₹85 crore** by Sunday night.

> "If there were no support from outside factors, the real collections would have been much lower but honest." — Trade analyst on Cocktail 2's inflated numbers



> **"Trade insiders have noted that Cocktail 2's numbers carry some "external push" — a diplomatic way of saying the reported figures may be partially inflated."**


That asterisk is worth acknowledging. Trade insiders have noted that Cocktail 2's numbers carry some "external push" — a diplomatic way of saying the reported figures may be partially inflated. But even with a conservative reading, this is comfortably Shahid Kapoor's biggest theatrical success since the ₹379-crore rampage of *Kabir Singh* in 2019.

## The Chemistry Equation

Director **Homi Adajania** — who helmed the original — understood the assignment. The 2012 film worked because it made you feel things for three people simultaneously, and the sequel replicates that alchemy with a new trio.

**Kriti Sanon** plays the grounded centre to **Shahid**'s restless energy and **Rashmika Mandanna**'s luminous warmth. The casting is inspired: Rashmika, making her biggest Bollywood play yet after dominating the South, brings a naturalism that makes every frame she's in feel effortless. Shahid, meanwhile, looks like a man who remembers what it feels like to have a hit — there's a looseness to his performance that's been missing since *Kabir Singh*.

The music has helped. Much like the original's soundtrack became a cultural staple ("Tumhi Ho Bandhu" still plays at every desi wedding), Cocktail 2's album has found traction, particularly in the diaspora where the nostalgia factor is real.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZzKzDcNIhc/


## The Battlefield Ahead

Here's where it gets complicated. **Welcome to the Jungle** arrived on June 26 with one of the widest releases in recent Bollywood history. Akshay Kumar's multi-starrer comedy is competing for the same screens, the same weekend audiences, and the same multiplex slots that Cocktail 2 needs to push past ₹100 crore.

The screen squeeze is real. Distributors have reportedly demanded all shows in single screens for Welcome to the Jungle, with a minimum of three shows per screen in 6+ screen multiplexes. That leaves Cocktail 2 fighting for scraps in its second weekend — precisely when it needs momentum.

The math: Cocktail 2 needs roughly **₹25 crore more** from here to join the ₹100-crore club. With Welcome to the Jungle eating screens and **Alpha** (Alia Bhatt's YRF spy thriller) arriving July 3, the window is narrow. But it's not shut.

## What It Means for the Diaspora

For NRI audiences, Cocktail 2 is still screening widely across the US, UK, and Canada. The overseas gross is estimated at roughly **₹24 crore**, boosted by the nostalgia factor — the original *Cocktail* was a defining film for a generation of diaspora millennials who saw themselves in its Goa-to-real-life love triangle.

The theatrical window is likely two to three more weeks before an OTT announcement drops. **Maddock Films** and **Luv Films** will be watching the ₹100-crore threshold carefully before deciding timing.

## The Bottom Line

Cocktail 2 isn't a blockbuster. It's something rarer — a mid-budget romantic film that found its audience in a month designed to destroy mid-budget romantic films. In a June that's already produced nine major releases, over ₹1,400 crore in collective stakes, and some genuinely brutal screen battles, Homi Adajania's film is still standing.

Shahid Kapoor needed this. Bollywood's romantic comedy needed this. And frankly, the audience that's been drowning in spy universes and action franchises needed a film that just wants you to fall in love with three flawed people for two hours.

The ₹100-crore question is still open. But honestly? It almost doesn't matter anymore.
